Stop 1 of 8

1 min read English

Virupaksha Temple

Living faith across centuries

Begin where Hampi has never stopped: a temple to Shiva that has held daily worship since long before the empire rose around it.

Photo: Vedamurthy J (CC BY-SA 3.0)

The gopuram above you is the tallest thing in Hampi for a reason. Virupaksha was here before Vijayanagara, a small shrine on the Tungabhadra, and it was still here after the city fell. Kings extended it, armies passed it, ruin spread around it, and the lamps stayed lit. When you step into the courtyard you are joining a queue of worshippers that has not broken in roughly fourteen centuries. Look for the pinhole image in the inner chamber, where light through a small opening throws the main tower upside down on the wall: an accident of architecture the temple has kept as a gift.

About this route

Vijayanagara, the city the world knew as Hampi, was one of the largest cities on earth in the sixteenth century. This walk crosses it from the temple that never stopped praying to the hill the empire watched its enemies from, taking in the bazaar where Persian horses were sold and the enclosure where kings reviewed their armies.
